subject: Standard operating procedure — f00 platform as a whole (GitHub + Cloudflare only)
opening: f00 is not one app. It is the brand hub (https://f00.sh), a product catalog, a shared theme, and the edge/DNS map for every f00-sh product. Public hosting is Cloudflare only. Source control is GitHub only. GitHub Actions may build and push to Cloudflare; GitHub does not host the sites. This SOP defines the whole platform so operators stop confusing “Pages” (Cloudflare Pages) with “GitHub Pages.”

sections.heading: 1. Purpose and scope
sections.body:
This procedure covers the f00 platform end-to-end: org inventory, hub laws, catalog SSOT, shared theme, Cloudflare DNS/Pages/R2, GitHub Actions deploy paths, product enrollment, release-to-card rules, and known failure modes.

In scope: hub repo f00-sh/f00; product repos under org f00-sh; Cloudflare account that owns zone f00.sh and Pages/R2 projects.

Out of scope: deep product-internal build SOPs (f00tils ASM gates, clun SBCL matrix). Those remain in each product’s own docs. This document only states how products attach to the platform.
items: Hosting target: Cloudflare (Pages + R2 + DNS). Never GitHub Pages / *.github.io.
Code host: GitHub org f00-sh only.
Hub is a static brand landing (splash + product cards). Install UX lives on product sites.
Catalog file site/catalog.json is the single source of truth for product list + theme pointer.

sections.heading: 2. One-sentence mental model
sections.body:
GitHub holds git history and runs CI. Cloudflare serves every public URL users open. When a workflow is named “Deploy site (Cloudflare Pages),” the word Pages means Cloudflare Pages, not GitHub Pages.

If CI/CD is healthy, a git push of site assets triggers GitHub Actions, which calls wrangler pages deploy with CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN and uploads the static tree into a named Cloudflare Pages project. Custom domains on that project are the live product URLs.

figure.title: Platform map — GitHub to Cloudflare
figure.caption: Operator view of the f00 platform. Public traffic terminates on Cloudflare. GitHub Actions is the normal push path into Cloudflare Pages and R2.

sections.heading: 3. Inventory — domains, Pages projects, packages
sections.body: Account ID (ops reference): 2e192c2d18f485155ba294ae5c9e1177. Zone: f00.sh. Cloudflare Pages Git Provider is Off for all f00 projects; deployments are wrangler-driven (Actions or local OAuth), not Cloudflare’s native Git hook.
items: Also: www.f00.sh → same hub project.
Infra repos (not product cards): homebrew-tap, scoop-bucket, .github org profile.
Released products get a hub card. status=wip products appear in catalog/AGENTS only.

sections.heading: 4. Hub product laws
sections.body: The hub is intentionally thin. Do not grow it into a product app.
items: Hub only: splash + product cards. No hero shortcut buttons, fake terminal/boot log, or install blocks on f00.sh.
Release → card: only catalog status=released products appear on the landing grid. Update the catalog entry when a product ships again if copy or links change.
One set of links: cards are the only product navigation (site, repo, optional docs).
Public copy is product-only: never put agent process, org plans, DNS wiring, or internal preferences on the public site or public README.

Aesthetic (standard theme): every product site loads the catalog theme CSS first. Three fonts only — Onyx = branding/logo only; zine mono = body; chip mono = headers/footers/nav/domain chips. No handwriting fonts.
No secrets in git. API tokens and DNS keys stay in GitHub secrets / Cloudflare / local wrangler OAuth only.

sections.heading: 5. Catalog SSOT procedure
sections.body: Edit only site/catalog.json in the hub repo. Derived surfaces: hub product cards in site/index.html, README product table, AGENTS.md sister table, live https://f00.sh/catalog.json after hub deploy.

steps.text: Edit site/catalog.json (product fields, theme.css pointer, status, docs URL, pages_project).
Regenerate derived files.
Or verify without write (CI does this on hub deploy).
Commit catalog + regenerated files together. Push main to deploy hub.
If theme path version changed (for example f00-theme-12.css), update product index.html theme <link>s (enroll-product.py or manual) and redeploy each product site so live HTML points at the new path.

sections.heading: 6. Shared theme procedure
sections.body:
Theme CSS and Onyx live under hub site/theme/ and site/assets/fonts/. Product sites load the versioned URL from the catalog (path version, not query string). Cloudflare edge often ignores query-string cache busts and can SPA-fallback missing paths to HTML; always ship a new filename (f00-theme-N.css) when rules change.

Type roles (do not redefine in product CSS):
items: Onyx: .splash, .brand-mark, .f00-brand only. Header brand-mark uses open tracking and larger size; splash logo may stay tight.
Zine mono: body, paragraphs, forms, tables of prose.
Chip mono: h1–h3, nav, footer, domain chips, meta accents.
Mirror unversioned site/theme/f00-theme.css to the current versioned file when bumping.
Update site/_headers for CORS/cache on new theme/styles paths.
After first request of a not-yet-deployed path, custom-domain cache can poison HTML for minutes–hours. Prefer new path versions; purge zone cache if bare path stuck on text/html.

steps.text: Copy current theme to a new path version and edit rules.
Mirror to f00-theme.css; set catalog theme.css + css_path; run sync-from-catalog.py.
Point hub index.html + product index HTML at the new URL. enroll-product.py THEME_HREF must match.
Push hub first (theme must exist as text/css on f00.sh before products depend on it).
Verify Content-Type is text/css.
Push or wrangle each product site.

sections.heading: 7. Site deploy — GitHub Actions to Cloudflare Pages
sections.body:
Yes: CI/CD on GitHub push deploys sites to Cloudflare when secrets are present. No: that is not GitHub Pages hosting.

Each product (and the hub) has .github/workflows/pages.yml (name: Deploy site (Cloudflare Pages)). Trigger is push to main/master on site paths (and related files), or workflow_dispatch. Job uses cloudflare/wrangler-action@v3 with secrets CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN and CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID, command pages deploy <dir> --project-name=<Pages project> --branch=<default branch>.

Hub additionally runs python3 scripts/sync-from-catalog.py --check before deploy so drifted cards/README/AGENTS fail the deploy.

rows: FAILING — token not injected; use local wrangler until fixed

steps.text: Confirm change is under the workflow path filters (usually site/**).
Push to the default branch (hub/f00tils/cel/trn: main; clun: master).
Watch Actions for “Deploy site (Cloudflare Pages)”.
If deploy fails with missing CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, either add the secret to the repo or deploy manually:
Verify custom domain HTML references expected theme and Content-Type of theme CSS is text/css.
Do not enable GitHub Pages settings on any f00-sh repo. Do not publish to username.github.io.

sections.heading: 8. Package publish path (R2 / dist.f00.sh)
sections.body:
Binary products (f00tils, clun) publish installable artifacts to Cloudflare R2 bucket f00-releases. Release workflows build on tag, create a GitHub Release for humans/checksums, then wrangler r2 object put into f00-releases/{product}/current/ and versioned prefixes. Public base: https://dist.f00.sh/{product}/current/.

Web-only products (cel, trn, hub) do not use R2 packages. Their “ship” is the Pages deploy.

steps.text: Follow the product release workflow (tag + release.yml).
Confirm R2 objects exist under dist.f00.sh after the release job.
If the product is newly released for the first time, set catalog status=released, sync hub, push hub so the card appears.

sections.heading: 9. Enroll a new f00 product
sections.body: New products under the brand must enroll in the catalog and load the shared theme. Prefer house new-project workflow with f00:true.

steps.text: Create repo under org f00-sh (not a personal account).
Create Cloudflare Pages project; attach custom subdomain under f00.sh.
Add repo secrets CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN and CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID (same account as hub).
Add pages.yml that wrangler-deploys the site directory to the Pages project name.
Inject theme link and catalog entry.
Keep status=wip until a real release; then set released and sync hub cards.
Product CSS is layout-only. Load catalog theme CSS first. Do not recolor or reassign type roles.

sections.heading: 11. Required GitHub secrets (platform)
sections.body: Place these on every repo that deploys to Cloudflare (hub + each product + release publishers). Prefer org-level secrets with repo allowlists if available.
items: CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN — Account permissions: Cloudflare Pages Edit; R2 Edit if the repo publishes packages; Zone read as needed.
CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID — 2e192c2d18f485155ba294ae5c9e1177 for this org account.
Never commit tokens. Rotate if exposed.
Local operator fallback: wrangler OAuth login (pages write) when Actions secrets are broken — treat as temporary.

sections.heading: 12. Explicit non-goals and forbidden configurations
items: GitHub Pages source branch or gh-pages branch hosting for f00-sh products.
Cloudflare Pages Git integration as a second deploy path without removing Actions (double deploy chaos) — current standard is wrangler-from-Actions only.
Forked per-product brand colors or green phosphor as the org standard (standard is black/white three-font theme from hub).
Hub install instructions or product binaries hosted on the hub site.
Secrets in site/ or docs/ committed to git.
